key_insight: Wall-bounded anisotropy is transferred to inertial settling particles and persists across scales, so particle energetics cannot be assumed isotropic even in the nominally isotropic range.
engineering_relevance: This matters for reduced-order dispersion and continuum models of settling particles, especially in wall-bounded or externally forced flows where anisotropy can alter transport and two-way coupling.
method: Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian DNS of inertial particles in turbulent wall-bounded flow at moderate Reynolds number.
Derived an exact but unclosed scale-wise conservation law for particle-phase energetics.
Used asymptotic analysis to interpret how turbulence intensity, particle inertia, and settling shape anisotropic energy transfer.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates scale-wise particle energetics using direct numerical simulation data and compares the quasi-streamwise and vertical fluctuation components across turbulent scales.
watch_item: The conservation law is exact but unclosed, so practical models will need careful closure for anisotropic, non-local particle effects.
paper_title: Development and application of a multiphase Lagrangian structure function model in anisotropic turbulence
